title: Model companions: comparing theories through embeddings

based_on.title: Model Theory Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 77–78 (§6.3, companion definitions, Proposition 6.28 and Exercise 31; updated 2018-12-14)

summary: Compare theories by mutual embeddings of their models, prove uniqueness of model companions and complete linear orders by dense orders.
abstract: Every nonempty linear order can be enlarged to a dense linear order without endpoints by replacing each point with a copy of the rational order. Model companions put this example into a general setting: two theories are compared by whether each of their models embeds into a model of the other. If a theory in this comparison makes every embedding between its models elementary, it is a model companion; there can be at most one such companion up to equivalence. A stronger notion, model completion, also asks that naming an original model settle every sentence about its possible extensions. We prove these results and show that dense linear orders provide a model completion of strict linear orders, using quantifier elimination and an explicit order construction.
